Futures as of ~2:35 AM PT (TipRanks). 10Y ~5.13% in Asian trade (+1 to 2bp vs the Oct 20 9 AM PT brief's 5.11%). headlines.headline: Futures higher on earnings: Nasdaq 100 e-minis +0.50%, S&P 500 e-minis +0.22%, Dow e-minis +0.01% (as of ~2:35 AM PT).
headlines.why_it_matters: A tech-led bid into a heavy earnings day (Meta, Tesla, IBM, Lam Research, TI after the close; SpaceX's beat and SMCI's raised guide already in the tape) after Tuesday's rotation rally was led by non-tech names.

headlines.headline: SpaceX Q3: revenue $14.6B (+161%, vs ~$12.7-13B est), net income $4.4B ($0.35 EPS vs ~$0.13-0.16 est) - its first profitable quarter as a public company. Super Intelligence revenue $7.56B (+830% YoY) became the largest segment for the first time (52% of total); Starlink 13.6M subscribers; capex $19.6B; Q4 capex guided to $35-40B; $63B backlog; shares +8-10% overnight (~$160-162 vs $147.79 close). ~1.3B shares unlock Thursday Oct 22.
headlines.why_it_matters: The SI print is hard demand data for the AI-capex narrative the market spent last week repricing - but about 37% of net income came from below the operating line ($1.03B other income, $390M tax benefit, $198M net interest income), so the 'first profitable quarter' headline overstates operating leverage.

headlines.headline: Musk confirmed both Tesla and SpaceX boards have formed special committees of independent directors to explore a merger, at shareholders' request; Musk recused himself as a conflicted party, said no terms are agreed and it is 'not a certainty' (Tesla would need a majority of ALL outstanding shares to approve). TSLA +1.7-2% premarket. Tesla reports Q3 after the close (call 5:30pm ET; est ~$0.40-0.43 EPS on ~$27.9B revenue).
headlines.why_it_matters: A confirmed process around a merger that would fold the AI-compute story into Tesla - positive optionality, but Musk's own 'not a certainty' and the high shareholder-approval bar cap the premium until tonight's print lands.

headlines.headline: Meta reports after the close (call 4:30pm ET): est revenue ~$63.3B (+24% YoY), EPS est ~$5.74-6.58 vs $7.25 a year ago (which carried a one-time benefit). Fell 1.59% Tuesday to $694.25; edging +0.1-0.2% premarket.
headlines.why_it_matters: The setup is ad growth vs AI-capex spend: last quarter the stock fell 8% on free-cash-flow/capex concerns despite solid revenue, so guidance on FY27 capex (reaffirmed $125-145B) matters as much as the quarter.

headlines.headline: Netflix Q3: revenue $12.87B (+11.8%, in line), EPS $0.87 vs $0.82 est, operating margin 34.6%; but Q4 revenue guided to $13.44B (+11.5%) vs ~$13.52B est and Q4 EPS $0.67 vs $0.73 est; 2026 ad-revenue forecast cut to $2.7B from $3B; FY26 revenue narrowed to $51.1B (low end of prior range); shares -5.5-6% overnight, brewing a sixth straight post-print decline. Company fired its CCO and film chief and cut ~1,000 jobs (6%) last week.
headlines.why_it_matters: A textbook guide-down: the EPS beat is overshadowed by the slowest top-line growth in three years and a $300M ad-forecast cut that undermines the one growth lever investors were counting on.

headlines.headline: Super Micro raised preliminary fiscal Q1 revenue guidance to $18.5-19.5B (from $14.5-15.5B) and gross-margin guide to 12-12.5% (from 10.4-10.8%); full results Nov 3; shares +12-17% overnight. The AI-hardware complex is bidding in sympathy: NVDA +1.9% premarket, MU +3%, SNDK +3.2%, plus neo-clouds CRWV/NBIS/IREN +4-5% overnight.
headlines.why_it_matters: A hard demand print from the AI-rack builder lands on the same tape as SpaceX's SI beat - together they argue the AI-infrastructure selloff was a positioning event, not a demand break; the Nov 3 full print is the real test.

headlines.headline: Salesforce signed a definitive agreement to acquire Braze for $47.50/share cash, ~$5.66B enterprise value (58% premium to Monday's close); funded entirely in cash, expected to close in Salesforce's fiscal 2028 with no change to FY27 outlook. BRZE +51.7% Tuesday to $45.57; CRM flat.
headlines.why_it_matters: Upgrades yesterday's single-source report to confirmed: Salesforce's third AI-marketing deal this year (after Qualified $1.2B and Fin $3.6B) shows enterprise-software M&A appetite is alive even as the market debates AI-capex returns.

headlines.headline: Oil bid again: Brent ~$109.6-110.1 (+1%), WTI December ~$98.6-99 (+0.8-1.1%) after a supertanker caught fire striking a sea mine south of the Strait of Hormuz and Houthis claimed attacks on Saudi Aramco's Yanbu site, the Shaybah oilfield, and Riyadh/Abha airports; Kpler counts at least 18 vessel attacks in two weeks, with attacks spreading to the Gulf of Oman. Iran's FM said Tehran has had no response to its peace-talks offer.
headlines.why_it_matters: The supply-risk premium is back after Tuesday's mediation-led dip (Brent settled $108.79, WTI Nov expired at $101.79): every escalation headline re-tightens the inflation tail the 10Y is pricing.

headlines.headline: 10Y Treasury 5.11-5.13% (+1-2bp in Asian trade) with $13B of 20-year supply today at 10 AM PT; markets price ~83-85% odds the Fed holds at the Oct 28 decision (LSEG/FedWatch), with three hikes fully priced over the next 12 months; EIA petroleum report 7:30 AM PT. Japan September exports rose 16.7% (missing estimates); BOJ seen holding Oct 30 before a December hike.
headlines.why_it_matters: Rates are the lid on multiples: a steady 10Y above 5.1% into supply keeps the multiple-expansion door shut no matter what earnings print.

headlines.headline: Loop Capital downgraded Apple to Hold from Buy, cutting its target to $330 from $370, saying ~13M iPhones removed from second-half 2026 shipments will not be made up in 2027 and flagging gross-margin pressure from rising memory costs (2027 EPS estimate cut to $9.76 from $10.11); MoffettNathanson also cut its target to $283 from $304 (neutral). AAPL -1% Tuesday to ~$342.50 after a record $343.46 close Oct 16; Apple event Oct 28, fiscal Q4 Nov 2.
headlines.why_it_matters: The year's best-performing Mag 7 name (+26% YTD) is being re-underwritten on units and margins: a falling iPhone shipment read gives the tape a reason to rotate away from hardware into tonight's AI-capex prints.

usac.why_it_matters: No fresh USAC headlines. Carried forward: Q3 $0.525/unit cash distribution declared Oct 15 (record Oct 26, paid Nov 6; $2.10 annualized, ~8.4% yield); Q3 results due before the open Tuesday Nov 3 with an 11am ET call; Q2 beat ($0.31 vs $0.28 EPS; revenue $342.15M vs $340.49M est; net income $45.7M); 34.5M Class A units (9.25% fixed, non-convertible, non-redeemable, non-listed) issued Oct 1 in the J-W Energy reorg; listing moved NYSE to TXSE Oct 5; $600M of 6.750% senior notes due 2035 issued September 2026; analyst consensus Hold (avg target $29.50); shares ~$24.88 Friday Oct 16. WTI December ~$98.9 (+1.1%) is a mild sentiment backdrop for compression demand, not company news.

analysis: What changed versus the Oct 20 9 AM PT post-open brief: (1) SpaceX flipped the AI-capex repricing on its head - SI revenue of $7.56B (+830% YoY, 52% of total) plus SMCI's raised preliminary guide gives the tape two hard demand prints against last week's selloff, and the confirmed Tesla-SpaceX merger-committee process adds a Tesla-side catalyst hours before its own print. Caveat: ~37% of SpaceX's net income came from below the operating line, so the profitability headline overstates operating leverage, and ~1.3B shares unlock Thursday. (2) Netflix is the anti-SpaceX: EPS beat but guide-down on everything that matters (ad forecast -$300M, Q4 EPS guide below consensus, slowest top-line growth in three years) - a sixth straight post-print decline is brewing, validating the GM/GE 'beat and fall' pattern. (3) Salesforce-Braze upgraded from single-source to confirmed (definitive agreement, Dow Jones/company PR): all-cash $5.66B, closes FY2028 - enterprise-software M&A is real even amid AI-capex skepticism. (4) Oil is two-way again: Tuesday's mediation-led dip reversed on the Hormuz mine strike and Houthi Saudi-infrastructure claims, with Brent back near $110; note the WTI roll (Nov expired $101.79, Dec front ~$98.9). (5) Rates are the lid: 10Y ~5.12-5.13% into today's 20-yr auction, Fed hold ~83-85% priced for Oct 28. (6) Megacap setup tonight is META on ad-growth-vs-capex and TSLA on margins plus merger optionality; Deepwater's Munster puts merger odds at 95% within two years (via X, single-source) against Musk's own 'not a certainty'. Signal vs noise: SpaceX numbers, merger committees (multiple outlets), Netflix numbers, SMCI preannounce, CRM-BRZE deal (company announcement + Dow Jones), oil attacks (Reuters), and rates/Fed data are confirmed; the Micron Taichung-union deal (Reuters via TipRanks) and Musk's $1T-2028 revenue chatter (Stocktwits) are single-source so far.

community_signals.takeaway: Aggregated sentiment from ~1,500 r/wallstreetbets daily-thread comments: SPCX's SI beat and the Tesla-merger committees dominate the tape; SMCI's raised preliminary guidance sparked a +17% overnight retail bid that spread into SOXL, MU, SNDK, NVDA, MRVL and neo-clouds (CRWV, NBIS, IREN); NFLX's guide cut drew broad disappointment. Retail is leaning long the AI-infrastructure tape into Meta and Tesla prints tonight.
